findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are ignored. With no surrogate, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers, which includes every public read-write member under name-based string keys without inspecting MessagePackObject, Key, or IgnoreMember. A referenced type annotated with [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember] therefore gets the wrong wire format, directly violating the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile ProjectA.MyObject into a metadata reference with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored. Generate a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class in Project B and inspect the emitted partial formatter: it should use ReadArrayHeader for the integer-key contract and should not access Ignored. On head it instead emits a string-key formatter containing both members.

findings.claim: The fallback for key types without an explicitly registered hash-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. Untrusted hash-based collection deserialization consequently accepts arbitrary custom key types with potentially collision-prone hashes, enabling the hash-collision denial-of-service attack that this guard and its adjacent comment exist to prevent.

receipt_plan.detail: Expose MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> through a test subclass and invoke it for a non-whitelisted custom key type, or deserialize a hash-based collection with that key type using MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. The existing security contract requires TypeAccessException; head returns/uses the default equality comparer instead.
